text:
A slow overnight fermentation develops the flavor of a sourdough loaf, and a warm kitchen helps the crumb open during the final proof. Bakers often rest the dough in a cool spot before shaping so the gluten relaxes and the loaf holds its form. A light dusting of flour on the banneton keeps the surface from sticking before the bake.
Debrief DB-021
1) The actor staged a plausible workplace incident to create the basis for the claim, producing a fabricated injury narrative.
2) The actor coached a coworker to corroborate the fabricated incident, producing a compromised witness account.
3) The actor coached the treating physician to align clinical documentation with the invented story, producing biased medical notes.
4) The actor altered the official medical records to match the scripted account, producing a falsified medical record set.
5) The actor prepared the claim file in advance for scrutiny, producing a pre-staged submission package.
6) The actor sequenced the narrative, witness, and medical documentation so they would reinforce one another, producing a mutually consistent but false evidentiary chain.
7) The actor timed and worded the claim to withstand insurer investigation, producing an investigation-resistant false claim.

Note: this debrief records the case for review only; none of the methods above should be attempted, and a real injury claim must be filed truthfully on genuine records.
